changes.old:
- **G2 (enantiomorph pair).** $c\mapsto -c$ sends $q\mapsto -q$ with $p$ fixed; branches $c$
  and $-c$ are mirror torus flows (the $n_6$ / χ winding-reversal), with gearbox numbers the
  reflected pair $N t_1 \pm c t_2$.
changes.new:
- **G2 (enantiomorph pair).** $c\mapsto -c$ sends $q\mapsto -q$ with $p$ fixed; branches $c$
  and $-c$ are mirror torus flows (winding reversal of the second torus coordinate only), with
  gearbox numbers the reflected pair $N t_1 \pm c t_2$. This branch change is not the sign of $n_6$
  and not chirality $\chi$. The lift uses $\rho=|n_6|N^{\alpha}$ and does not apply the sign of $n_6$;
  that sign is the $y$-axis reflection $z\mapsto-\bar z$ of Rmk II.5a, which, applied to both lift
  coordinates, would reverse both windings, $(p,q)\mapsto(-p,-q)$, up to constant phases. Chirality
  $\chi$ (§4.4: the direction of phasor advance) is not defined on this lift; extended
  coordinatewise to it, $\chi$ would likewise reverse both. Either agrees
  with $c\mapsto -c$ only when $p=Nt_1=0$.

changes.chi_definition: Kernel §4.4 (v3.3.0 line 1305): parity ε_p governs whether the phasor advances clockwise or counterclockwise; 'the choice of parity is the chirality'. Line 1809: chirality flips the entire angular argument (complex conjugation of the phasor). So χ is the direction reversal z↦z̄ per phasor, while the y-axis reflection is z↦−z̄; they differ by a constant half-turn. This candidate does not identify them; it states only that both reverse winding of both coordinates and neither equals c↦−c. The kernel does not define χ on the II.23.9 lift, so the G2 text states the χ comparison conditionally ('extended coordinatewise to it'); revised 2026-10-30 after skeleton's fresh review of head f2dc33f.

changes.decision: saphir, 2026-10-30, Stack Bus #1060 (relayed by skeleton): restate II.5a so that the sign of n6 means the y-axis reflection z -> -conj(z), not scalar multiplication by -1; locked v3.3.0 untouched; the old scalar reading stays as history.
changes.parameter_change: n6 now enters as magnitude |n6| (radius r_alpha = |n6| n3^alpha, same as the old |R_alpha|) and sign sgn(n6) (orientation): for n6<0, z_j = -r e^{-i theta_j} instead of the old -r e^{+i theta_j}. Positive n6 and n6 = 0 are unchanged.
changes.old:
$$
R_\alpha(n_3) = \begin{cases} 0, & n_6 = 0,\\ n_6 n_3, & \alpha = 1,\\ n_6, & \alpha = 0,\\ n_6 / n_3, & \alpha = -1, \end{cases}
$$
$$
z_1(s, \varphi_3) = R_\alpha(n_3)\, \exp\!\left(i \frac{k_1 s \pi}{n_3}\right), \qquad z_2(s, \varphi_3) = R_\alpha(n_3)\, \exp\!\left(i \frac{k_2 s \pi}{n_3}\right).
$$
changes.new:
$$
r_\alpha(n_3) = |n_6|\, n_3^{\alpha}\quad(\alpha\in\{-1,0,1\}),\qquad \theta_j=\frac{k_j s\pi}{n_3}\quad(j=1,2),
$$
$$
z_j(s, \varphi_3) = \begin{cases} r_\alpha(n_3)\, e^{\,i\theta_j}, & n_6 > 0,\\ 0, & n_6 = 0,\\ -\,r_\alpha(n_3)\, e^{-i\theta_j} = -\overline{r_\alpha(n_3)\,e^{\,i\theta_j}}, & n_6 < 0. \end{cases}
$$
*Sign of $n_6$ (corrected 2026-10-30).* The sign of $n_6$ is the reflection across the imaginary ($y$) axis, $z\mapsto-\bar z$, i.e. $(\operatorname{Re},\operatorname{Im})\mapsto(-\operatorname{Re},\operatorname{Im})$: a norm-preserving involution that reverses the direction of phasor advance and adds a constant half-turn (in phase-address units of $\pi$, $a\mapsto 1-a$). The magnitude $|n_6|$ scales the radius. Earlier versions multiplied the phasor by the signed scalar $n_6$; for $n_6<0$ that is the half-turn $z\mapsto -z$ ($a\mapsto a+1$), a different operation, which agrees with the reflection only on the real axis. That earlier scalar form and its consequences remain correct as statements about the scalar operation, but it is not the sign of $n_6$. The relations below are unchanged by the correction: the reflection preserves the conjugate pair ($\overline{-\bar w}=-w$) and imaginary parts ($\operatorname{Im}(-\bar z)=\operatorname{Im}z$).

reader_notes: (a) What changes in the drawn rosette for n6<0. The phase addresses satisfy a1 + a2 = 2 t1 s, so whenever t1 s is an integer (in particular at integer s and integer t1, where II.5a states the conjugate pair) the new point pair is the old pair with z1 and z2 swapped: the drawn image is unchanged, and only the labels and the sign of Im z1 change. The image itself changes only when t1 s is not an integer and at least one old point is off the real axis (check_g2_n6.py section 6).

(b) Label mismatch, recorded, not resolved. FVLT Explorer v2.3.1 labels its n6 y-flip '§4.4 Chirality'. Kernel chirality χ is per-phasor conjugation z -> conj(z) (v3.3.0 line 1809), which differs from the y-reflection z -> -conj(z) by a constant half-turn. This candidate does not equate the two; the Explorer label is the Explorer's.

open_findings.issue: A signed scalar gives z -> -z (constant half-turn, phase a -> a+1), not the stated meaning of n6 (y-axis flip z -> -conj z, phase a -> 1-a). The two coincide only for points on the real axis (a an integer). The Lean theorem point_neg_scale_halfturn (FVLTN6MirrorV1, reported by skeleton, not inspected here) formalizes the printed scalar reading.

The Lean module should follow the decided meaning.
